Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
COMMERCIAL STEEL WOOL 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope - ■ Covers the requirements for commercial steel wool of different grades. 

2. Grades- — The commercial steel wool shall be o1 the following yrades' 

Grade 0000 ( Super fine ) 
Grade 000 C Extra fine ) 
Grade 00 ( Very fine) 
Grade ( Fine ) 
Grade 1 ( Medium ) 
Grade 2 ( Coarse } 
Grade 3 ( Very coarse ) 

3. Width of Steel Wool Fibres — Shall bt; in accordanco with Table 1, when tested at. in 7.1 

4. General Requirements 

4.1 Individual fibres shall have uniform sharp cutUrg edges and the edges of fibres shall not be blunt, 
when examined (jnder a microscope of magmfrcation 50 X, 

4.2 The length of the fibres shall be such that wool will cling together in handling without excessive 
unravelling 

4.3 Finished wool shall present a smooth uniform <ippearance The fibres shall be free from saw-teeth, 
ruggedness spirals or whirls, when examined under a mannification of 50 X 

5. Material — Steel wool j^hnll be produced frorr* suitable carbon steel ur alloy steels meeting the 
requirements laid down jn 7.4 

6. Manufacture - Steel wool shall be of uniform, thm, long fibre strands of steel havinq sharfi, 
smooth cutting edges and shall be free from chips, short ends and materials other than stftel fibres^ 
examined under a magnification of 50 X, 

7. Tests 

7.1 Width of Fibre - A specimen of 20 fibres shall bo selected at random from a lot Ench fibre shall 
be measured under a 50 X magnification nucroscope. graduated in micrometres. Not more than one 
fibre in each specimen shall have a width less than the values specified in col S of Table 1 Not 
more than one fibre in each specimen shall have a wrdlh greater than the values specified in col 4 of 
Table 1 and if this one fibre has width greater than the values specified in col 5 of Table 1 the 
specimen shall be declared as fail 

7.2 Ductility — A single fibre of each grade of steel wool shall be capable of wmdrng in a singly loop 
tightly around the mandrel of size 15 mm in diameter 

7.3 Moisture and Oil Content — The loss in mass of a 50 g sample of steel wool after drying m an 
oven at 120"C for an hour, shall not exceed 1'5 percent. 

7.4 Corrosion Resistance 

7.4.1 For steel wool { used for piteralion purposes) - Prepare a mtric acid solution by adding 5 ml 
concentrated nitric acid and 95 ml of dtstilled water. Put two drops of this solution on a compressed 
tuft of the steel wool and observe tor any evidence of corrosion attack. Steel woo! shall not show 
sign of corrosion attack.

8. Sampling 

8.1 Unless otherwise atjteed between the supplier and the purchaser, the procedure dS given in 
*S ' 2500 (Part 1 }-f973 'Samplfng rnspeclfon tables Pdit f Irrspection by attnbutes dnd by count of

APPENDIX A 

INTENDED USES OF COMMERCIAL STEEL WOOL 

A-1. Sieel wool complyjng with this specification is intended to be used as an abrasive material for 
the following purposes; 

Grade 0000 For rubbing down paint, varnish, polish or shellac belore fmal coat on any surface 
for quality job

Grade 000 For fine work on anodized surfaces and rubbing down paint, varnish, etc. Also on 
furniture before polishing and for aluminium utensils. In dairies, for bottles and 
stainless steel equipment 

Grade 00 For fine polishing of suriaces and household uses. 

Grade For polishing and huffing surfaces. 

Grade 1 For cleaning of motal surfaces and light stripping of floor waxes and polishes, and 
for the preparation of wood surfaces for frrst coats or fillers 

Grade 2 For general abrasive cleaning, for example, removal of rust and old paint, and 
rapid stripping of floor waxes and polishes. 

Grade 3 For heavy abrasive cleaning, and smoothing of rough surfaces Also for cleaning 
of rubber moulds In tyre factorfes, cleaning of bottoms of ships 

A-2. Steel wool of grades 1, 2 and 3, also meeting the requirements of 7.4.1 are used for filteration 
purposes in the chemical industry 



EXPLANATORY NOTE

dimensions of width of steel woof fibres with th*; otiier nationel specifications. The optujn for use of 
material for manufacture of steel wool has been made provided it meets the test requirements and 
accordingly typ«s have been deleted-
